questions.question: The price of the three varieties of rice, dal 1, dal 2 and dal 3 is Rs. 22/kg, Rs. 24/kg and Rs. 30/kg, respectively. If the ratio in which the quantity of dal 1, dal 2 and dal 3 is mixed to form a mixture is 5:3:2, respectively, then find the price per kg of the mixture.
questions.explanation:
Let, quantity of dal 1 = 5 kg

Quantity of dal 2 = 3 kg

And, Quantity of dal 3 = 2 kg

CP of dal 1 = 5 x 22 = 110Rs

CP of dal 2 = 3 x 24 = 72 Rs

CP of dal 3 = 2 x 30 = 60 Rs

So, Total CP = 110 + 72 + 60 = 242 Rs

Hence, Price per kg of the mixture = \(\frac{242}{5 + 3 + 2} = 24.2\) Rs

questions.question: 132 litres of a mixture (milk + honey) contains milk and honey in the ratio 7: 4, respectively. If a certain quantity of the mixture is replaced with 54 litres of honey, then the ratio of quantity of milk to that of honey in the final mixture becomes 2 : 5. Find the quantity of the mixture that has been replaced.
questions.explanation:
Initially,
Quantity of milk in 132 litres of mixture=711×132= 84 litres
Quantity of water in 132 litres of mixture=411×132= 48 litres
Let the quantity of Milk and Honey taken out be '7x ' litres and '4x ' litres, respectively.
According to question:

84-7x48-4x+54=25

Or, 420 – 35x = 96 – 8x + 108 

Or, 35x – 8x = 420 – 204 

Or, 27x = 216 

Or, x = 8 

Quantity of mixture that has been replaced = 7x +  4x = 11x = 11 × 8 = 88 litres

questions.question: A Seller deals in milk and 90 litre mixture is to be distributed in Milk and Water in the ratio of 5:4. If 40 litre milk and 20 litre water will be added in the mixture then what will be the new ratio of water and milk?
questions.explanation:
Quantity of milk\(\  = \frac{5}{9} \times 90\  = \ 50\ l\)

Quantity of water \(= \ 90 - 50\  = \ 40\ l\)

After adding 40 l of milk and 20 l of water;

Quantity of milk \(= 40 + 50 = \ 90\ l\)

Quantity of water\(\  = \ 20 + 40 = \ 60\ l\)

New ratio\(\  = \ 90:60\  = 3:2\)

questions.question: 480 litres of a mixture contain milk and water, only, in the ratio of 5:x, respectively. If 20 litres water is added into it, then the ratio of quantity of milk to that of water in the resultant mixture will become 3:2. Find the value of ‘x’.
questions.explanation:
Total quantity of resultant mixture = 480 + 20 = 500

Quantity of milk in resultant mixture = (3/5) × 500 = 300 litres

Quantity of water in resultant mixture = 500 – 300 = 200 litres

Since, quantity of milk remains constant. So, quantity of milk in initial mixture = 300 litres

And, quantity of water in the initial mixture = 480 – 300 = 180 litres

O, ratio of quantity of milk and water in the initial mixture = 300:180 = 5:3

So, x = 3

Hence, option e.

questions.question: In a mixture of milk and water, the proportion of water by weight was 75%. If in 60 gm of mixture 15 gm water was added, what would be the percentage of water? (weight in gm)

questions.question: In a mixture, the ratio of the juice to water is 8 : 3 . If 22 litres of the mixture is removed and replaced by 8 litres of water, the ratio of juice to water becomes \(8: 5\). What was the total quantity of the initial mixture?
questions.explanation:
Let the quantity of the juice in the initial mixture \(=\) \(8 x\) litres
Quantity of the water in the initial mixture \(=3 x\) litre
According to the question,

\[
\begin{aligned}
& \frac{8 x-22 \times \frac{8}{11}}{3 x-22 \times \frac{3}{11}+8}=\frac{8}{5} \\
& \Rightarrow 5(8 x-16)=8(3 x-6+8) \\
& \Rightarrow 40 x-80=24 x+16 \\
& \Rightarrow 16 x=96 \\
& \Rightarrow x=6
\end{aligned}
\] Total initial quantity of the mixture \(=6 \times 11=66\) litres

questions.question: A vessel contains 300 liters mixture of milk and water and contains 60% milk. If x liters of water is added to the mixture, so the ratio of milk to water in the final mixture becomes 4:3, find the value of x.?
questions.explanation:
Quantity of milk \(= \ 60\%\ of\ 300\ l = \ 180\ l\)

Quantity of water\(\  = \ 300 - 180\  = \ 120\ l\)

As per question; \((120 + x):180 = 3:4\)

\( 480 + 4x = 540\)

\( 60 = 4x\)

\( x\  = \ 15\)

A container contains a mixture of milk and water in ratio of 8:7. Now, 50% of the mixture is taken out and in the resultant mixture quantity of milk is 5 litres more than the quantity of water. Find the Initial quantity of Milk in the mixture.
questions.explanation:
Let the quantity of milk and water be 80x and 70 x respectively.

So; initial quantity \(= \ 80x + \ 70x\  = 150x\ l\)

After replacing 50% of the mixture, i.e.\(\ (50\%\ of\ 150 = 75x\ l\));

Quantity of milk \(= \ 80x - \frac{8}{15} \times 75x = 40x\)

Quantity of water\(\  = \ 70x - \frac{7}{15} \times 75 = 35x\)

As per question;

\(Quantity\ of\ milk\  = \ 5\  + \ Quantity\ of\ water\)

\(= > 40x = 5 + 35x\)

\(= > x\  = \ 1\)

Hence, initial quantity of milk \(= \ 80\ x = \ 80\ l\)

questions.question: A vessel contains milk and water in the ratio of 9 : 5 respectively. If 10 liters of water added to the mixture, the ratio of milk to water becomes 3 : 2. Find the quantity of milk initially present in the vessel.
questions.explanation:
Given Information:

  • Initial ratio of milk to water = 9 : 5
  • 10 liters of water is added to the mixture
  • New ratio of milk to water = 3 : 2

Calculation:

Let the initial quantities of milk and water be
Milk = 9x liters
Water = 5x liters

After adding 10 liters of water:
New quantity of milk = 9x
New quantity of water = 5x + 10

According to the question, the new ratio is 3 : 2

So,
9x / (5x + 10) = 3 / 2

Cross-multiply:
18x = 15x + 30

18x − 15x = 30
3x = 30
x = 10

Initial quantity of milk
= 9x
= 9 × 10
= 90 liters

questions.question: A mixture of alcohol and water contains 45% water. If the total cost of alcohol present in the mixture at the rate of Rs. 42/litre is Rs. 4158, then find the additional amount of water to be used in the mixture such that the quantity of milk and water becomes same.
questions.explanation:
Let, Total initial quantity of mixture = “x” Litres

Quantity of water in mixture =

\(45\%\ of\ x = \frac{45}{100}of\ x = 0.45x\)

Quantity of alcohol = (100 – 45) % of x = \(\frac{55}{100}\ of\ x = 0.55x\)

Also, quantity of alcohol = \(\frac{4158}{42} = 99\)L

So, 99L = 0.55x

x = 180

Let, “y” amount of water is added, then ATQ

0.45x + Y = 0.55x

=> 0.10x = y

=> 0.10(180) = y

=> 18L = y

questions.question: The proportion in which two kinds of tea, one costing Rs. 44 and the other costing Rs. 39, should be mixed so that the mixture can be sold at Rs. 42 is -
questions.explanation:
Let they are mixed in proportion m: n

So, 44m + 39n = 42\(\times\) (m + n)

44m + 39n = 42m + 42n

2m = 3n

So, m:n = 3:2

questions.question: A container contains milk and water in the ratio of 7:8. If 20 litre of milk is replaced with water then the new ratio becomes 1:2, then find the total sum of the mixture initially.
questions.explanation:
Let milk and water be 7x and 8x l.

Quantity of milk after replacing \(= \ 7x - 20\ l\)

Quantity of water after replacing \(= \ 8x + 20\ l\)

As per question;

\((7x - 20):(8x + 20) = 1:2\)

\( 14x - 40 = 8x + 20\)

\( 6x = 60\)

\( x = \ 10\ l\)

Therefore; total quantity of mixture \(= \ 8x + 7x = 15x = 150\ l\)

questions.question: A container contains 60 litres of milk. From this container 5 litres of milk were taken out and replaced by water. This process was repeated further two times. Remaining milk is how much percent of the mixture in the container.(approx)
questions.explanation:
Quantity of milk \(= 60\ l\)

Quantity of milk replaced\(= \ 5l\)

After further 2 times;

Milk left\(\  = \ 60(1 - 5/60)^{3}\)

\(= 60(\frac{55}{60})^{3}\)

\(= 46.21\ l\)

So; percentage of milk\(\  = \ \frac{46.21}{60} \times 100 = 77\%\)

questions.question: In a tank the ratio of A and B is 10:9 and a person replaces 19 liters of mixture from the tank with C and the ratio of A,B and C becomes 90:81:19. Find the total quantity of A initially in the tank.
questions.explanation:
Let the quantity of A and B be 10x and 9x l respectively.

When 19 l is replaced;

Quantity of A left\(\  = \ \frac{10x - \ 10}{19} \times 19 = \ 10x - 10\ l\)

Quantity of B left\(\  = \frac{\ 9x - 9}{19} \times 19 = \ 9x - 9\ l\)

Quantity of C\(= 19\ l\)

As per question:

A:B:C \(= \ 90:81:19\)

\(= > 10x - 10:9x - 9:19 = 90:81:19\)

So;

\(= > 9x - 9:19 = 81:19\)

\(= > 9x - 9 = 81\)

\(= > x = 10\ l\)

So; initial quantity of A\(\  = \ 10x = 100l\)

questions.question: At the Old Monk Company four drums of similar size are filled with Alcohol. The alcohol content in the four drums is 40%, 37%, 30% and 25% respectively. If all four mixtures are mixed, what will be the ratio of water and alcohol in the mixture obtained?
questions.explanation:
Quantity of alcohol in 1st drum = \(\frac{40}{100}\)

So, quantity of water in 1st drum = 1 - \(\frac{40}{100}\) = \(\frac{60}{100}\)

Quantity of alcohol in 2nd drum = \(\frac{37}{100}\)

So, quantity of water in 2nd drum = \(\frac{63}{100}\)

Quantity of alcohol in 3rd drum = \(\frac{30}{100}\)

So, quantity of water in 3rd drum = \(\frac{70}{100}\)

Quantity of alcohol in 4th drum = \(\frac{25}{100}\)

So, quantity of water in 4th drum = \(\frac{75}{100}\)

Quantity of alcohol & water in final mixture

= (\(\frac{40}{100} + \frac{37}{100} + \frac{30}{100} + \ \frac{25}{100}\)) : (\(\frac{60}{100}\)+\(\frac{63}{100}\)+\(\frac{70}{100}\)\(+\)\(\frac{75}{100}\))

= (\(\frac{33}{25}\):\(\frac{67}{25}\)) = (33:67)

Hence, required ratio = 67:33

Percentage of water in new mixture \(=\frac{378}{728} \times 100\)
